overview: Expedia Group is a global online travel agency (OTA) holding company operating a portfolio of consumer travel brands (Expedia, Hotels.com, Vrbo, Orbitz, Travelocity, ebookers, Wotif) alongside a fast-growing B2B travel-technology platform and a majority stake in trivago, a hotel metasearch business. The company facilitates roughly $131-132 billion of annual gross bookings (FY2026E) across lodging, air, car rental, cruises, insurance, and activities for travelers worldwide, monetizing primarily through merchant and agency commissions on hotel/lodging transactions plus a growing advertising business. Expedia operates in nearly 50 countries with approximately 3.9 million lodging properties available (2.5 million alternative accommodations via Vrbo, 1.4 million hotels/other via its other brands) as of Q3 2026.

business_model.summary: Expedia earns revenue chiefly through its B2C segment (Expedia, Hotels.com, Vrbo and other legacy brands) and its faster-growing B2B segment (Expedia Partner Solutions / Rapid API / TAAP agent booking tool / white-label platform), supplemented by trivago's third-party metasearch advertising. Revenue is largely transactional (commission on bookings) rather than subscription-based, though the One Key loyalty program and growing advertising revenue add some recurring, high-margin characteristics. FY2025 revenue was $14.7 billion (B2C 70% merchant / 22% agency / 8% advertising by business model split); through nine months of FY2026, revenue reached $12.68 billion (+13% YoY), with B2B revenue growing materially faster (+24% YoY) than B2C (+7% YoY). Lodging is by far the largest service type (~80-81% of revenue), with air (~2-3%), advertising (~8%), and other travel products (insurance, car rental, cruise, activities) rounding out the mix.

revenue_streams.name: Lodging (hotel + Vrbo alternative accommodations)
revenue_streams.trend: growing - core driver, ~11-12% YoY in Q3 2026

revenue_streams.name: B2B / Expedia Partner Solutions (Rapid API, TAAP, white-label)
revenue_streams.trend: growing strongly - segment revenue +24% YoY YTD 2026, now ~35% of total revenue vs ~28% in FY2025

revenue_streams.name: Advertising & Media (EG Advertising + trivago)
revenue_streams.trend: growing - trivago advertising +36% YoY YTD 2026 on brand-rebuild, EG Advertising +11% YoY

revenue_streams.name: Air
revenue_streams.trend: declining - bookings and revenue pressured by reduced global air capacity (Middle East disruptions) in 2026

revenue_streams.name: Other (insurance, car rental, cruise, activities)
revenue_streams.trend: growing - insurance and activities revenue up materially in 2026

business_model.customer_type: Primarily B2C leisure travelers globally (via Expedia, Hotels.com, Vrbo, Orbitz, Travelocity, ebookers, Wotif) plus a large and growing B2B customer base of airlines, offline travel agents, online retailers, corporate travel management firms and financial institutions that license Expedia's supply and technology (Rapid API, TAAP, white-label/co-branded templates, optimized distribution for wholesale rates)
business_model.geographic_mix: Global operations across nearly 50 countries with approximately 16,000 employees; reporting currency is USD with material foreign-exchange exposure to EUR, GBP, JPY, AUD, BRL and CAD. Specific revenue-by-geography breakdown is not separately disclosed in recent filings, but international markets (lower-margin in some cases) represent a meaningful and growing share of bookings, particularly through B2B expansion.

main_competitors: Booking Holdings (Booking.com, Priceline, Kayak, Agoda, OpenTable)
Google (Google Travel, Google Flights, Hotel Ads)
AI agent platforms (OpenAI/ChatGPT, Google Gemini, Amazon, Perplexity) offering agentic travel search and booking
competitive_position.market_position: One of the world's largest online travel companies, but management itself notes gross bookings represent only a single-digit percentage of Phocuswright-estimated $2+ trillion global travel spend in 2026, underscoring a long runway alongside intense competition. Historically a close #2 to Booking Holdings in Western OTA share (the two together estimated at roughly 40%+ of global OTA gross bookings as of 2024), with Expedia's B2B/Partner Solutions business a distinguishing growth engine versus Booking's more B2C-weighted model. Vrbo is a top-tier alternative-accommodation brand in North America but trails Airbnb's global scale (Airbnb lists far more properties worldwide than Vrbo's ~2.5 million).

moat_factors.description: Migrated Hotels.com and Vrbo front-ends onto the Brand Expedia stack in 2023, creating a single shared infrastructure (search, payments, fraud, customer service, data centers) that improves feature velocity and cost efficiency across brands and benefits the B2B business as well.

Rapid API, TAAP and white-label solutions let banks, airlines, offline agents and other travel platforms tap into Expedia's lodging supply (~3.9 million properties). B2B gross bookings grew 19-21% YoY in recent periods, materially outpacing B2C, and higher revenue margins (13-15% vs 11-13% for B2C) suggest a structurally advantaged, harder-to-replicate business line.

moat_factors.factor: Scale of supply and brand portfolio
moat_factors.description: Approximately 3.9 million lodging properties and relationships with 500+ airlines give Expedia negotiating leverage and breadth versus smaller players, though it trails Booking Holdings (28 million+ listed properties, largely via Booking.com's aggressive direct-signing model) in raw property count.

Cross-brand loyalty (Expedia, Hotels.com, Vrbo) launched in the US (2023), UK (2024) and expanded further in 2025-2026, intended to increase direct/repeat traffic and reduce dependence on paid search. Still maturing versus Booking Holdings' and hotel chains' own loyalty ecosystems; a July 2026 tiering change (reducing base OneKeyCash earn rate from 2% to 1% for entry-tier members) drew member criticism, a sign the program's economics are still being tuned.

Early public partnerships embedding Expedia inventory into ChatGPT, Claude, and (in progress) Gemini, plus Perplexity Comet and Amazon Alexa+ voice booking, position Expedia to capture bookings redirected through AI agents rather than be disintermediated by them -- though this is unproven and could cut either way.

weaknesses: Smaller scale than Booking Holdings in market cap (~$32-35B vs ~$140B+) and property count, with less diversified brand portfolio (Booking's OpenTable/Agoda/Priceline add adjacent revenue Expedia lacks)

High and rising reliance on paid search/marketing: selling and marketing-direct remains the largest cost line (44-50% of revenue), leaving Expedia structurally exposed to Google algorithm or pricing changes and to escalating customer-acquisition costs

Vrbo's roughly 2.5 million alternative-accommodation listings are dwarfed by Airbnb's global inventory, limiting Expedia's share of the fast-growing alternative-accommodations category outside North America
Air segment structurally low-margin and shrinking (revenue -7% YoY in Q3/9M 2026) amid airline consolidation and direct-connect technology adoption that pressures Expedia's remuneration

Barry Diller's concentrated Class B voting control (~32% of total voting power via ~4.6% of shares) and recent leadership transitions create governance and succession-risk considerations for investors

growth_drivers: B2B / Expedia Partner Solutions continues to be the primary growth engine: gross bookings +19-21% YoY and revenue +18-24% YoY in recent periods, now representing roughly a third of total segment revenue and carrying higher revenue margins than B2C

Advertising business re-acceleration: trivago returned to sustained growth after a multi-year brand-rebuilding effort (advertising revenue +33% in FY2025, +36% YoY YTD through Q3 2026) and EG Advertising growing low-double-digits as the sponsored listings/display business scales

Agentic AI / LLM distribution: partnerships embedding Expedia booking capability directly into ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity Comet and (in progress) Google Gemini, plus opening Rapid API-style access so AI agents can query Expedia inventory natively -- a bet that owning supply/fulfillment matters more than owning the search interface as travel search shifts toward conversational AI

One Key loyalty program expansion: continuing international rollout (UK since 2024, additional Brand Expedia markets through 2025-2026) intended to deepen direct relationships and reduce paid-marketing dependency over time

Continued platform unification and AI-driven internal efficiency: shared front-end/back-end infrastructure plus AI-assisted customer service and developer productivity initiatives are structurally reducing cost of revenue and technology/content expense as a percentage of revenue (cost of revenue fell from 12.3% of revenue in FY2023 to 9.9% in FY2025 to 9.5% YTD through Q3 2026)

Large and reinstated capital return program: $0.48/share quarterly dividend (reinstated 2025) plus a newly authorized $5 billion buyback program (May 2026, on top of the existing 2023 authorization) aggressively shrinking share count and lifting EPS (diluted shares outstanding fell from ~133 million to ~122 million YoY through Q3 2026)

business.description: Management explicitly flags that the rapid emergence of generative and agentic AI could intensify competition from technology companies and new entrants deploying AI-driven travel search/planning/booking, potentially reducing direct-booking rates and raising marketing costs as Expedia competes for visibility within AI interfaces it does not control. Google's increasing prioritization of its own Google Travel/Flights/Hotel Ads in search results compounds this risk.

Competes against Booking.com, Airbnb, metasearch sites (Kayak, TripAdvisor, trivago itself), and travel-supplier direct-booking channels that increasingly offer loyalty perks, exclusive inventory and better pricing to bypass OTAs entirely.

business.risk: Dependence on travel-supplier and GDS relationships
business.description: A substantial portion of revenue depends on negotiated compensation with lodging suppliers, airlines and GDS partners (Amadeus, Sabre); suppliers could reduce commissions, restrict access, or push direct-connect technology that bypasses Expedia's economics.

Short-term rental regulation is proliferating globally, including the EU Short-Term Rental Law effective May 2026 requiring registration numbers for all EU alternative accommodations; could reduce Vrbo listings and raise compliance costs.

financial.description: Significant exposure to EUR, GBP, JPY, AUD, BRL and CAD; hedging programs mitigate but do not eliminate currency risk, particularly around the timing gap between booking and stay for accommodation revenue.

$6.3+ billion of outstanding long-term debt as of Q3 2026 (recently refinanced via a new $1B 5.5% notes issuance in April 2026 and a new $2.5B revolving credit facility through March 2031); a credit-rating downgrade would raise borrowing costs on certain outstanding notes.

financial.risk: Negative free cash flow in Q3 2026
financial.description: Operating cash flow of negative $1.16 billion and free cash flow of negative $1.40 billion were reported for the quarter (largely working-capital/seasonal and investment-timing driven), a reminder that Expedia's merchant-model cash generation is seasonally volatile and sensitive to a slowdown in the merchant hotel business.

financial.risk: Aggressive capital returns relative to cash generation
financial.description: $1.7-1.9 billion of share buybacks plus $173 million of dividends YTD through Q3 2026, alongside $1.8 billion used to redeem maturing notes, places ongoing demands on liquidity; the company retains an essentially untapped $2.5B revolver as a backstop.

regulatory.description: In Q3 2026 the IRS replaced and expanded its prior transfer-pricing adjustments (2011-2016) and issued new adjustments for 2017-2018, now proposing a combined ~$1.0-1.2 billion in additional federal income tax, subject to interest, across 2011-2018. Expedia disputes the adjustments and is contesting through administrative procedures; an adverse resolution would be financially material.

Italian withholding tax dispute (GdF audit alleging ~150 million euro / $175 million unpaid withholding tax for 2017-2023) resulted in reserves of $90 million (Q3 2025) plus $88 million additional (Q4 2025); evolving digital services taxes and OECD base-erosion initiatives create ongoing multi-jurisdiction tax uncertainty (though Canada's DST repeal in March 2026 allowed a $71 million reserve reversal in 2026, a rare favorable resolution).

regulatory.risk: Global alternative-accommodation and OTA display regulation
regulatory.description: EU Digital Services Act, EU AI Act, EU Short-Term Rental Law (effective May 2026), US FTC Rule on Unfair or Deceptive Fees (effective May 2025), and a patchwork of US state/local short-term-rental ordinances raise compliance costs and could restrict listings or require new disclosures.

regulatory.risk: Antitrust/competition scrutiny of parity clauses and marketplace practices
regulatory.description: Historical and ongoing investigations by national competition authorities (e.g., Australian Competition and Consumer Commission ruling against trivago's Australian website practices) into hotel-rate parity clauses and marketplace conduct.

macro.risk: Travel demand cyclicality and geopolitical shocks
macro.description: Q1-Q2 2026 results were negatively affected by events in the Middle East and Mexico and reduced European air capacity; Q4 2026 guidance reflects softer demand tied to the US election cycle and continuing Middle East/Europe tension, illustrating how quickly discretionary travel demand reacts to geopolitical and macro shocks.

Travel is discretionary; slow growth, high unemployment, inflation, tighter credit or higher interest rates are all cited by management as factors that have historically and could in the future reduce travel demand and booking value.

Reduced global air capacity (Middle East disruptions) drove air ticket prices higher but ticket volumes down in 2026; average daily hotel rates (ADRs) fluctuate with supply growth and macro conditions, directly affecting Expedia's percentage-based revenue.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Phocuswright estimates global travel spending (inclusive of alternative accommodations and tours/activities) at over $2 trillion in 2026; online travel penetration continues to grow but is already high in the US and Western Europe, with emerging markets (Latin America, Eastern Europe) representing the larger incremental opportunity. Industry observers (e.g., Skift) expect the next decade of OTA growth to be slower and more competitive than the last, with margin pressure from AI-native competition and direct-booking strategies by suppliers.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderately high. Revenue and bookings are sensitive to macro shocks (geopolitical conflict, recession, pandemics), seasonal (strongest in Q3, weakest in Q1), and historically severely impacted during the COVID-19 pandemic, from which the business model has since fully recovered and re-scaled.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate indirect sensitivity via consumer discretionary spending and via Expedia's own cost of debt ($6.3B+ outstanding, with new issuance at 5.4-5.5% coupons reflecting the current rate environment); working-capital float from the merchant model (float invested at interest income) provides a modest offsetting tailwind to higher rates.
key_input_costs: Traffic-generation/search-engine marketing costs (the largest single expense line)
Payment processing and card-network interchange fees
Personnel (especially AI/ML and software engineering talent)

recent_developments.event: Q3 2026 earnings reported: revenue $4.94 billion (+12% YoY), gross bookings $34.0 billion (+11% YoY), Adjusted EBITDA $1.69 billion (+17% YoY), operating income $1.33 billion (+28% YoY), net income attributable to Expedia $1.03 billion (+7% YoY), diluted GAAP EPS $8.42 (+15% YoY) and Adjusted EPS $9.39 (+24% YoY). Results beat the company's own August guidance across bookings, revenue and Adjusted EBITDA. Despite the beat, shares fell roughly 8.5% in after-hours trading as Q4 2026 bookings guidance (3.3-5.2% growth) implied the slowest quarterly growth in six quarters, with management citing softer early-Q4 demand tied to the US election cycle, continuing Middle East/Europe disruption, a fall promotional sale that shifted into September, and tough B2B comparisons against large partner promotions in Q4 2025.

Full-year 2026 guidance raised: gross bookings to $131.4-131.9 billion (~10% growth, up from $129.5-130.8 billion) and revenue to $16.37-16.43 billion (up from $16.05-16.22 billion); expected Adjusted EBITDA margin expansion widened to 1.8-2.0 points for the year (from a prior 1.5-1.75 points), implying FY2026 will show materially better operating leverage than FY2025.

Board declared a $0.48/share quarterly dividend payable December 10, 2026 (record date November 18, 2026), consistent with the per-share rate paid throughout 2026 (up from $0.40/share in 2025, the first full year dividends were reinstated after a multi-year pause).

IRS replaced and materially expanded its prior transfer-pricing adjustments: new proposed federal tax liabilities of approximately $287-313 million (2011-2013), $488-531 million (2014-2016), and $213-380 million (2017-2018) -- roughly $1.0-1.2 billion combined, versus the prior $675 million claim. Expedia disputes the adjustments and continues administrative defense; the IRS indicated 2019-2020 are not relevant to this matter.

Canada enacted 2026 federal budget legislation retroactively repealing the Digital Services Tax Act back to June 20, 2024, allowing Expedia to reverse $71 million of previously accrued Canadian DST liabilities during the first nine months of 2026 -- a rare favorable tax development after several years of rising digital-tax exposure.

Audit Committee authorized an additional $5 billion share repurchase program (the '2026 Share Repurchase Program'), layered on top of the existing 2023 $5 billion authorization; combined, $5.1 billion remained available for repurchase as of September 30, 2026, after $1.5-1.7 billion of buybacks executed in the first nine months of 2026.

Issued $1 billion of new 5.5% senior unsecured notes due 2036 (net proceeds ~$986 million), and in February 2026 redeemed/settled the maturing $750 million 5.0% senior notes and the $1 billion 0% Convertible Notes (including a ~$78 million conversion premium paid to noteholders); in March 2026 replaced its revolving credit facility with a new $2.5 billion facility maturing March 2031.

Expanded AI/agentic distribution strategy: launched a ChatGPT plugin (October 2025) letting users move from itinerary planning in ChatGPT directly to booking on Expedia.com; extended booking integrations to Anthropic's Claude; began running ads inside ChatGPT (February 2026); and opened Expedia's inventory more broadly so AI agents from OpenAI, Google, or Amazon can query it natively, alongside a Perplexity Comet partnership (OneKey Silver status for Comet users) and Amazon Alexa+ voice booking. CEO Ariane Gorin has said Expedia is also working to appear within Google's Gemini. Management maintains that AI-driven search 'isn't going to impact' core travel-agent (TAAP) business, framing AI agents as a new distribution channel rather than a existential threat.

One Key loyalty program restructured its OneKeyCash earn rate by tier (Blue 1%, Silver 2%, Gold 2%, Platinum 3%, versus a flat 2% previously for all members), effectively reducing earn rates for entry-tier (Blue) members -- drawing criticism from loyalty-program commentators as a program devaluation even as it is framed internally as better rewarding frequent travelers.

Continued multi-year restructuring/reorganization program (initiated February 2024) to recalibrate headcount following completion of the company's platform/technology transformation; recognized $104 million of charges in the first nine months of 2026 (compared to $76 million in the same 2025 period), with roughly $10 million of additional charges expected.

Raised from $16.05-16.22 billion prior guidance; implies roughly 11-12% full-year revenue growth versus FY2025's $14.73 billion.

items.target: +1.8 to +2.0 percentage points of margin expansion
items.notes: Widened from a prior 1.5-1.75 point expansion range; would represent materially better operating leverage than the margin gains reported in FY2025 (Adjusted EBITDA margin rose from 21.4% in FY2024 to 23.8% in FY2025).

The lowest quarterly bookings growth guidance range in six quarters, reflecting softer early-Q4 demand (US election cycle, Middle East/Europe disruption), a fall sale that shifted into September, and tough B2B comps against large Q4 2025 partner promotions.
Consistent with the bookings deceleration guided for the quarter.
Seasonally the lowest-bookings quarter of the year per Expedia's typical seasonality pattern (revenue/income lowest in Q1, highest in Q3).

items.notes: Most of the previously flagged FY2026 restructuring has already been recognized ($104 million through nine months).

Dividend reinstated in Q1 2025 after a multi-year pause; raised 20% for 2026.

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Ariane Gorin on Q3 2026 results: 'We exceeded the high end of our guidance in the quarter, reflecting resilient travel demand and strong execution.' CFO Derek Andersen flagged 'much tougher comps in the second half of the year' ahead of the Q3 print, which materialized as softer Q4 guidance tied to US election-cycle demand softness, continuing Middle East/Europe disruption, a fall sale that moved earlier into September, and difficult B2B comparisons against large Q4 2025 partner promotions. On AI, management (including Gorin) has characterized agentic AI partnerships (ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity Comet, Amazon Alexa+, and in-progress Google Gemini integration) as incremental distribution opportunities rather than existential threats to the B2B/TAAP travel-agent business, while simultaneously flagging in risk-factor disclosures that failure to navigate the 'agentic revolution' effectively could have a material adverse effect on the business.

bull_case: B2B / Expedia Partner Solutions is a structurally advantaged, faster-growing, higher-margin business (revenue +18-24% YoY, revenue margins of 13-15% vs 11-13% for B2C) that is steadily increasing its share of total company revenue and insulates Expedia from some of the direct B2C competitive pressure facing Booking Holdings and Airbnb

Aggressive, well-funded capital returns: a newly doubled buyback capacity ($10 billion combined authorization, $5.1 billion remaining) alongside a growing dividend are shrinking the share count materially (diluted shares down from ~133 million to ~122 million year-over-year) and directly driving EPS growth (Adjusted EPS +24% YoY in Q3 2026) even when bookings growth is more modest

Early, broad-based AI/agentic distribution positioning across ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and (in progress) Gemini could let Expedia capture bookings redirected through AI search even as traditional organic/paid search referrals face disruption -- a proactive rather than defensive posture relative to some peers

Margin expansion is accelerating and broad-based: cost of revenue, technology/content, and G&A have all fallen as a percentage of revenue for three consecutive years, and FY2026 Adjusted EBITDA margin expansion guidance (1.8-2.0 points) was raised mid-year, evidence that platform-unification and AI-driven efficiency initiatives are delivering real operating leverage

Reasonable valuation discipline: despite a ~$32-35 billion market cap versus Booking Holdings' ~$140 billion+, Expedia trades at a steep discount while posting comparable or better YoY growth in several recent quarters, and sell-side price targets (most dated mid-2026, ranging roughly $270-$390) imply meaningful potential upside from current levels
bear_case: Q4 2026 bookings guidance of only 3.3-5.2% growth -- the slowest in six quarters -- combined with an 8.5% after-hours stock decline on an otherwise strong Q3 beat, signals the market is increasingly focused on decelerating forward momentum rather than trailing results, and tougher year-over-year comparisons could persist into early 2027

Escalating IRS transfer-pricing dispute now totals roughly $1.0-1.2 billion in proposed additional federal tax liability (up from ~$675 million previously), subject to interest, and an adverse resolution -- even partial -- would be a material cash and earnings event layered on top of ongoing Italian withholding-tax and other international tax exposures

Agentic AI is a double-edged sword: while Expedia has moved early to embed its inventory in ChatGPT, Claude and other AI agents, the company's own risk disclosures concede that a failure to navigate the 'agentic revolution' as well as competitors, or a consumer shift toward AI-native platforms where Expedia lacks presence (e.g., deeper OpenAI/Google-native booking flows that bypass Expedia's supply entirely), could materially and adversely affect results

Heavy and rising B2B partner-commission costs (selling and marketing-direct +15% YoY in Q3 2026, driven specifically by B2B partner commissions) raise the question of how much of B2B's faster revenue growth is translating into incremental profit versus simply being a lower-margin pass-through business at scale

Negative free cash flow reported for Q3 2026 (-$1.40 billion) alongside an aggressive, debt-funded capital-return program (new 5.5% notes issued even as $1.8 billion of maturing notes/convertibles were redeemed) raises questions about the sustainability of the current buyback pace if travel demand or working-capital dynamics deteriorate in a downturn
